To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is a low risk of neurotoxicity in occupationally solvent exposed workers in the Federal Republic.
there are no neurotoxic risks for workers with solvent-exposed jobs, if they are exposed to solvent concentrations which are below the threshold limit values of the TRGS 910.
the neurotoxic effects of organic solvents are low and that they are not detectable with current neurobehavioral tests.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether there is evidence of an association between exposure to solvents and the development of a toxic encepalopathy, and if so, what are the factors that may explain these findings.
the question of whether there is an occupational risk for the neurobehavioral performance of solvent-exposed workers.
the neurotoxic effects of solvents and solvent combinations in painters and spraypainters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neurotoxic effects of organic solvents are still not well defined.
neurotoxic risks from solvent exposure in painters cannot be excluded.
neurotoxic effects of solvents in occupationally solvent exposed workers are unlikely.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need of a better definition of the neurotoxicity of solvents and a better understanding of the mechanisms of neurotoxicity.
the neurotoxicity of solvents has not been proven, but cannot be excluded.
the neurobehavioral effects of solvent exposure are not as dramatic as they are often assumed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neurotoxicity is not a problem of the past, but is still a major problem in the present.
the neurotoxicity of organic solvents is a complex issue, which requires further research.
the results of the epidemiological and occupational medicine studies do not support a high neurotoxic risk in painters and spray-painters.
